newsitem.title: USA: Prab buys back stock from Michigan.
newsitem.headline: Prab buys back stock from Michigan.

text.p: Prab Inc said it reached an agreement it which it repurchased certain of its shares held by the State of Michigan Retirement Systems (SMRS).
The shares include 600,000 of non-convertible preferred stock, 1,633,333 shares of convertible preferred stock and 1,013,770 shares of common stock.
An additional 52,897 shares of common stock were purchased from SMRS by Prab's profit sharing plan.
To finance the repurchase, Prab said it borrowed $2.7 million from a bank, used cash on hand and borrowed $680,000 from unsecured lenders.
Prior to the transaction, Prab had 2,647,860 shares of common stock outstanding. After closing the agreement on October 31, it had 1,757,340 shares of common stock outstanding.
Outstanding convertible preferred stock was reduced to 366,667 shares from 2,000,000. Outstanding non-convertible preferred stock of 600,000 shares was entirely eliminated.

Prab president Gary Herder, in a statement, called the repurchase a positive move for the future of the company's shareholders. He note Prab's sales have grown to an estimated $15 million for fiscal 1996 from $8.9 million in fiscal 1993.
Prab manufactures conveyors, metal scrap reclamation systems and bulk material handling equipment.
